listings.name: Cancer Services Program (free mammograms, Pap tests)
listings.description: Free breast, cervical and colon cancer screening if you have no insurance or your insurance won't cover it.
listings.eligibility: NY resident; uninsured, high deductible, or coverage doesn't pay; meet income limits. Mammogram 40+ (or under 40 if high risk); Pap/pelvic exam 40+; stool test 50+.
listings.notes: Run from St. James Mercy Hospital (Hornell) for Steuben, Allegany, Cattaraugus and Chautauqua counties, with local staff. Follow-up tests free if eligible.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Health Dept - Cancer Services Program

listings.name: The Chautauqua Center - Jamestown (prenatal & family planning)
listings.description: Community health center with prenatal and OB/GYN care, birth control, STI testing. Sliding fees, takes Medicaid, uninsured welcome.
listings.what_to_bring: Photo ID and proof of income (for sliding fee)
listings.notes: OB/GYN-maternal care from HRSA-based directory; NYS facility record lists family planning and prenatal services for TCC Jamestown (older address). Holds 'Mammogrammy' expedited mammogram events in October.
listings.source_name: Black Health directory (HRSA data)

listings.name: GLPP Women's Health (UPMC Chautauqua)
listings.description: Gynecology office. Birth control including IUD, shot and implant; Pap tests; yearly exams.
listings.notes: Prenatal care and births are at UPMC Chautauqua Maternity Care Center, 207 Foote Ave, Jamestown (hospital main line 716-487-0141). Insurance accepted not listed; sliding fee not stated.
listings.source_name: UPMC website

listings.name: Planned Parenthood - Buffalo Health Center
listings.description: Abortion, birth control, STI testing and treatment. Telehealth visits by phone/video available. Sliding fees, takes Medicaid.
listings.hours_text: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9am-5pm; Wed 11am-7pm; closed weekends
listings.schedule_note: Alternating Fridays 7:30am-5pm
listings.notes: OUTSIDE Chautauqua County (about 1-1.5 hrs from Dunkirk/Jamestown). No Planned Parenthood or abortion provider found inside the county. Appointment required.
listings.source_name: Planned Parenthood website

listings.name: Salvation Army ANEW Center - Rape Crisis Program
listings.description: Free, confidential help after sexual assault or rape. 24-hour hotline.
listings.notes: Office line 716-661-3894. Same agency runs domestic violence services; no address listed on purpose. County calls 800-252-8748 the 24-hour 'Hotline for Rape & Battering'.
listings.source_name: NYS Office for Prevention of Domestic Violence directory

listings.name: Chautauqua County Social Services - Jamestown Office
listings.description: County social services office. Apply here for SNAP (food stamps), Medicaid, cash assistance, emergency help with rent, utilities, heat or shelter, and HEAP.
listings.what_to_bring: Birth certificates or other ID for you and your family; Social Security numbers for everyone; proof of rent or mortgage; fuel or utility receipts; pay stubs if working; proof of other income; bank statements and other resources; if you have a disability, signed consent for your doctor to fill out a medical form.
listings.eligibility: Based on income and resources. You do not need to be getting ongoing assistance to ask for emergency help.
listings.notes: Medicaid line for this office: 716-661-8219. HEAP line: 716-661-8103. You can also apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov. Applying for cash assistance also applies you for Medicaid and SNAP. Upload documents with the free NYDocSubmit app. County lists 24-hour Crisis Helpline 800-724-0461 for after-hours emergencies; for emergency shelter after hours call the Sheriff at 716-753-4232.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Chautauqua County Social Services - Dunkirk Office
listings.description: County social services office in north county. Apply for SNAP (food stamps), Medicaid, cash assistance, emergency help and HEAP.
listings.what_to_bring: Birth certificates or other ID for you and your family; Social Security numbers for everyone; proof of rent or mortgage; fuel or utility receipts; pay stubs if working; proof of other income; bank statements and other resources; if you have a disability, signed consent for your doctor to fill out a medical form.
listings.eligibility: Based on income and resources.
listings.notes: HEAP line at this office: 716-363-3544. Emergency shelter help during business hours: 716-679-9881 (per county Code Blue page). Some older county pages (SNAP, Application Information) still list 319 Central Ave, Dunkirk; the Temporary Assistance, Medical Assistance, HEAP and Code Blue pages list 15 W. Lucas Ave. Call to confirm before going.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Chautauqua County Dept. of Mental Hygiene & Social Services - Mayville
listings.description: County social services offices in the Hall R. Clothier Building in Mayville. Child and Adult Protective Services are here. Also a daytime warming center.
listings.address: 7 N. Erie Street, Hall R. Clothier Building
listings.notes: Phone 716-753-4421 is listed for this site on the county Code Blue warming center list; Child and Adult Protective Services: 716-753-4104. County's general Social Services number: 716-753-4998. Benefit applications (SNAP, Medicaid, cash) are handled at the Jamestown and Dunkirk offices per the county program pages.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: SNAP (Food Stamps) - Chautauqua County
listings.description: Apply for SNAP online at mybenefits.ny.gov, by phone (ask for a paper application), or in person at the Jamestown or Dunkirk office. You can hand in an application the same day with just your name, address and signature.
listings.what_to_bring: Proof of identity (birth certificate, driver license or other ID); Social Security numbers for everyone applying; proof of where you live and housing costs (lease, rent receipt, or mortgage/tax/insurance); pay stubs or employer statement; proof of other income (Social Security, unemployment, child support, pension, veterans benefits); child care and medical bills if you have them.
listings.eligibility: Based on household income and expenses. Expedited (fast) benefits may be issued within 5 days if you qualify.
listings.notes: Dunkirk: 716-363-3500. Fax applications to 716-661-8225. SNAP email: Dssfs@chqgov.com. An interview by phone or in person is required; you choose which. Benefits count from the day you file. Decision within 30 days.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Nutrition Outreach (NOEP) - SNAP application help
listings.description: Free help filling out a SNAP (food stamps) application. Walk-ins and appointments.
listings.notes: Toll-free: 877-686-9209. Listed on the county SNAP page.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Emergency Assistance - Chautauqua County Social Services
listings.description: Help if you are homeless, have little or no food, have an eviction notice, are out of heating fuel, have a utility shutoff notice, or are not safe at home. Can help with back rent, utility bills, fuel, and temporary shelter.
listings.eligibility: You do not need to be on ongoing assistance to get emergency help. Programs for SSI recipients (EAA), families with children or pregnant women (EAF), and single adults/couples (ESNA).
listings.notes: Also at 15 W. Lucas Ave, Dunkirk. Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov or at either office. After hours, weekends and holidays, for emergency shelter call the Sheriff's Office at 716-753-4232 (county Code Blue page). 24-hour Crisis Helpline: 800-724-0461.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Social Security Office - Dunkirk
listings.description: Federal Social Security office for the area. Help with retirement, disability (SSDI), SSI, Medicare and Social Security cards.
listings.notes: Fax 833-950-3277. National line: 1-800-772-1213 (Mon-Fri 8am-7pm). SSA's official office list has no Jamestown office; some third-party directories show one at 321 Hazeltine Ave, Jamestown, but that address is the Jamestown VA Clinic. Many services can be started online or by phone, so call before going.
listings.source_name: Social Security Administration field office data

listings.name: Neighborhood Legal Services - Health Insurance Navigators
listings.description: Free, state-certified Navigators help you sign up for Medicaid, Essential Plan, Child Health Plus or other health plans through NY State of Health.
listings.notes: Chautauqua County Navigator line. NLS also has an online Request Help form. NY State of Health customer service: 1-855-355-5777 (Mon-Fri 8am-8pm, Sat 9am-1pm). Full navigator list by county is in the NY State of Health Navigator Directory.
listings.source_name: Neighborhood Legal Services

listings.name: NY State of Health - Customer Service
listings.description: New York's official health plan marketplace. Call to apply for or ask about Medicaid, Essential Plan, Child Health Plus and other health plans, or to find free local help.
listings.notes: TTY: 1-800-662-1220. Phone line, statewide.
listings.source_name: NY State of Health

listings.name: Free Tax Help (VITA) - United Ways of Chautauqua County
listings.description: Free tax return preparation by IRS-certified volunteers during tax season. Book by calling 2-1-1. Do not call United Way to book.
listings.hours_text: Seasonal (tax season, usually January-April). Call 211 to book.
listings.schedule_note: Seasonal. Sites change each year; 2025 sites were in Dunkirk, Jamestown and Silver Creek, with more added later.
listings.what_to_bring: Photo ID; Social Security cards for you, spouse and dependents (or ITIN letter); birth dates for everyone; all W-2, 1099 and unemployment statements; 1098-T/1098-E and 1095-A if you have them; last year's returns; bank routing and account number for direct deposit; daycare provider total paid and tax ID. For joint returns both spouses must be there to sign.
listings.eligibility: 2025 season: households earning $67,000 or less, people with disabilities, and people with limited English. (2023 season limit was $73,000; check current limit.)
listings.notes: Toll-free 1-888-696-9211, or text your zip code to 898211. Self-file free at MyFreeTaxes.com. Info from local news reports (Jan 2023, Jan 2025) about the United Way program; 2026-27 season details not yet published.
listings.source_name: Observer (Dunkirk) news, Jan 2025; WRFA news, Jan 2023

listings.name: HEAP Home Energy Assistance - Chautauqua County
listings.description: Help paying heating costs for homeowners and renters, including when heat is in your rent. Emergency HEAP helps if your heat or electric is about to be shut off or you are almost out of fuel.
listings.schedule_note: 2025-26 season: Regular HEAP Dec 1, 2025 - Apr 7, 2026; Emergency HEAP Jan 2 - Mar 31, 2026 (state memo says through Apr 7); Cooling Apr 15 - Jun 22, 2026. 2026-27 dates not yet announced by the state as of 2026-10-10.
listings.eligibility: Income-based. 2025-26 monthly gross income limits: 1 person $3,322; 2 people $4,345; 3 people $5,367; 4 people $6,390 (higher for bigger households). Money in the bank does not disqualify you. Emergency HEAP: bill must be in your name and you must live there; shutoff notice, or less than 10 days of fuel / under 1/4 of a 275-gallon tank.
listings.notes: Apply for Regular HEAP online at mybenefits.ny.gov (fastest). Emergency HEAP cannot be done online - call. Or call 716-661-8103 to get a paper application mailed. Mail to: HEAP Office, 110 East 4th Street, Jamestown, NY 14701. Dunkirk drop-off: 15 W. Lucas Ave (716-363-3544). Interviews are by phone. If you get SNAP or cash assistance, call your worker. State HEAP hotline: 1-800-342-3009.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: HEAP Heating Equipment Repair or Replacement (HERR)
listings.description: Repairs or replaces a broken main home heating system for older homeowners. The county must approve you before any work starts.
listings.schedule_note: Reopened Dec 11, 2025 until funds run out.
listings.eligibility: Homeowner age 60 or older (at least one person on the deed), owned and lived in the home as main residence for the past 12 months, and HEAP-eligible.
listings.notes: Apply at the Jamestown or Dunkirk social services office; staff will call you for an interview. For help, NY Connects: 716-753-4582.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: NY Public Service Commission - Utility Shutoff Hotline
listings.description: If your electric or gas is about to be shut off (48/72-hour final notice), call this state hotline. Contact your utility first and ask about a payment plan.
listings.notes: For a final shutoff notice, call - do not use the online form. Pay the part of your bill that is not in dispute while they investigate. Ask the utility about a Deferred Payment Agreement or Budget Billing. General complaints helpline: 1-800-342-3377 (Mon-Fri 8:30am-4pm). Also ask about Emergency HEAP (716-661-8103).
listings.source_name: NYS Department of Public Service

listings.name: Weatherization Assistance - Chautauqua Opportunities
listings.description: Free home weatherization to cut heating costs, starting with an energy audit. Homeowners and renters can apply.
listings.eligibility: Income at or below 60% of state median income (see HEAP income limits). Automatically eligible if someone in the home gets SSI, public assistance, SNAP or HEAP. Priority to seniors, families with children, and people with disabilities.
listings.notes: Hours and Jamestown address from the county Code Blue warming center list; program details from county Office for Aging article (Feb 2025). Dunkirk office: 10825 Bennett Rd, 716-366-8176.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.schedule_note: Activated at 32F or below including wind chill, Nov 1 - Apr 30. Get alerts: text CODEBLUECHQ to 898211.
listings.notes: 716-753-4232 is the Sheriff's Office for shelter after hours, weekends and holidays. During business hours: Jamestown DSS 716-661-8200, Dunkirk DSS 716-679-9881. 24-hour Crisis Helpline: 800-724-0461. Some sites may not allow pets (service animals OK), large bags, or sleeping.

listings.name: Chautauqua County DMV - Jamestown
listings.description: County-run DMV office. Get or replace a NY non-driver ID or driver license.
listings.what_to_bring: Completed form MV-44 and proofs of identity (6 points; see NYS DMV forms ID-44 / ID-82). Proof of date of birth and Social Security card (or proof you are not eligible).
listings.notes: Processing stops at 4:15pm. Real ID / Enhanced license upgrades, new permits or IDs, and out-of-state transfers must start by 3:15pm. Book an appointment online (individuals only). Replacing a license or ID costs $17.50 and needs 6 points of ID (NYS form ID-82). Veteran designation on license: bring original DD-214 with honorable discharge, no fee.

listings.name: Jamestown City Clerk - Birth Certificates
listings.description: Get a copy of a birth certificate in person or by mail. Going in person can be faster, sometimes same day.
listings.address: 200 East Third Street, Municipal Building, 1st Floor
listings.what_to_bring: Birth Certificate Request Form (download from the City Clerk page) and ID: driver license, non-driver ID, passport, naturalization papers, military ID, employer photo ID, OR two utility bills with your name and address. A police report of lost/stolen ID is also listed. Fee $30.
listings.eligibility: The person named on the record or a parent named on it.
listings.notes: Mailed copies usually take about 2 weeks. The page does not say which births it holds; call first to confirm they have your record (generally births registered in the city). Email: clerk@jamestownny.gov.
listings.source_name: City of Jamestown

listings.name: Dunkirk City Clerk - Birth Certificates
listings.description: Request a copy of a birth certificate from the Dunkirk City Clerk. The request letter must be notarized.
listings.what_to_bring: Full name at birth; date of birth; your phone number; photocopy of photo ID (state driver license preferred); NOTARIZED request letter; mailing address; $10 per copy by check or money order. If someone else picks it up, their name and relationship to you.
listings.notes: Phone and hours not listed on the source. Call first to confirm they hold your record.
listings.source_name: City of Dunkirk City Clerk

listings.name: NY State Dept. of Health - Vital Records (birth certificates by mail/online)
listings.description: Order a NY birth certificate (births outside NYC) online or by phone through VitalChek, or by mail to the state.
listings.address: P.O. Box 2602 (Vital Records Certification Unit) - mail only
listings.what_to_bring: Driver license, non-driver photo ID, US passport or US military photo ID - OR two of: utility or phone bills, or a government agency letter dated within the last 6 months. Mail form DOH-4380.
listings.eligibility: The person named on the certificate, a parent named on it, or a spouse/child/other person with a NY court order.
listings.notes: Fees: $45 per copy online/phone plus $8 vendor fee; $30 by mail (check or money order, no cash). VitalChek phone orders: 1-877-854-4481 (24/7, English and Spanish).
listings.source_name: NY.gov

listings.name: Replace a Social Security Card (free)
listings.description: Replacement Social Security cards are free. Start online if you can; otherwise call or make an appointment at the Dunkirk Social Security office. Card comes by mail in 5-10 business days.
listings.hours_text: Phone line Mon-Fri 8am-7pm; Dunkirk office Mon-Fri 9am-4pm
listings.notes: Local offices cannot print a card on the spot. TTY 1-800-325-0778. Dunkirk office phone: 888-862-2139.
listings.source_name: Social Security Administration

listings.name: LawNY (Legal Assistance of Western New York) - Jamestown
listings.description: Free civil legal help for low-income people in Chautauqua County: evictions and landlord problems, foreclosure, public benefits, family law, consumer debt, bankruptcy, unemployment, veterans issues.
listings.notes: Toll-free 866-664-4567. Fax 716-664-7179. Serves Chautauqua County. The best way to find out if they can help is to call. Online application also available on lawny.org. Also runs a pro se (do-it-yourself) divorce clinic.
listings.source_name: LawNY

listings.name: Chautauqua County Family Court
listings.description: Family Court for Chautauqua County (custody, support, orders of protection and more).
listings.address: 2 Academy Street, Suite 5, Chautauqua Municipal Building
listings.notes: The court page lists no help center or self-help office for this court. If you cannot afford a lawyer in a Family Court case, ask the court about the Family Court Public Defender.
listings.source_name: NY State Unified Court System

listings.name: Family Court Public Defender - Chautauqua County
listings.description: Free lawyers for eligible people in Family Court cases (support, abuse/neglect, paternity, family offenses and more). Cases come by referral from the court.
listings.eligibility: Referred by Family Court; you fill out a financial form from the court.
listings.notes: Main Public Defender's Office: Hall R. Clothier Bldg., 7 N. Erie St., Mayville, 716-753-4376, Mon-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm. Walk-in interview times listed: Dunkirk City Court (342 Central Ave) Mon 9am-noon; Jamestown City Court (200 E. 3rd St, 2nd floor) Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 9am-noon.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: NY State Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service
listings.description: Get matched with a private lawyer. Referral is free; first half-hour consultation is $35 (free for some case types like Social Security, veterans, unemployment).
listings.hours_text: Online request; contact within 5 working days
listings.notes: Requests are online only. A 211 directory lists Chautauqua among the 45 counties this service covers. 518-463-3200 is the general NYSBA number. Email lrs@nysba.org if not contacted within 5 working days. No separate Chautauqua County Bar referral service was found.
listings.source_name: New York State Bar Association

listings.name: Chautauqua County Veterans Service Agency - Jamestown
listings.description: Free county help for veterans and families: VA benefits claims, VA health care enrollment, burial benefits.
listings.notes: County page also lists the agency at 110 E. Fourth St., Jamestown (same phone) in one section - call to confirm location. Hours are listed on the county page under the Dunkirk office and may apply to both.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Chautauqua County Veterans Service Agency - Dunkirk

listings.notes: Address and hours from VA.gov. Phone 716-338-1511 is from the county veterans page, which still shows the old address (608 W. Third St.); VA.gov did not show a phone in our check.
listings.source_name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

listings.name: Dunkirk VA Clinic
listings.description: VA outpatient clinic: primary care, mental health, lab, pharmacy, x-ray and imaging, quit-smoking help.
listings.notes: Address and hours from VA.gov. Phone 716-203-6474 is from the county veterans page, which lists an older address (166 E. Fourth St.); VA.gov did not show a phone in our check - confirm by calling.
listings.source_name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

listings.name: Buffalo VA Medical Center
listings.description: Main VA hospital for Western New York.
listings.notes: Toll-free 800-532-8387. Erie VA Medical Center (135 E. 38th St., Erie, PA 16504, 800-274-8387) is also listed by the county.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County (official site)

listings.name: Erie Vet Center
listings.description: Free, confidential counseling for veterans, service members and families. Nearest Vet Center to south Chautauqua County; also has a mobile Vet Center.

Buffalo Vet Center: 2929 Union Road, Cheektowaga, NY 14227, Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm. Neither lists a Chautauqua County location; call about mobile visits.

listings.name: Chautauqua Works (American Job Center) - Jamestown

listings.name: Chautauqua Works (American Job Center) - Dunkirk

listings.name: County Social Services - Emergency Housing (Jamestown)
listings.description: Go here on weekdays if you have nowhere to stay tonight. Staff help set up emergency shelter or a motel. Also a daytime warming spot.
listings.eligibility: You do not need to be on ongoing Temporary Assistance to get emergency help.
listings.notes: County Emergency Assistance page lists 716-661-8200 and says it can cover temporary hotel/motel costs, back rent and utility arrears. After hours call the Sheriff at 716-753-4232. Can also apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: County Social Services - Emergency Housing (Dunkirk)

listings.eligibility: You do not need to be on ongoing Temporary Assistance to get emergency help.
listings.notes: Social Services main line is 716-753-4998. After hours call the Sheriff at 716-753-4232.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: County Social Services (Mayville)
listings.description: County social services office. Daytime warming spot on weekdays; can point you to emergency housing help.
listings.notes: Listed on the county Code Blue page as a daytime warming center (Hall R. Clothier Building). The county page names Jamestown and Dunkirk as the offices that arrange emergency shelter.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: After-Hours Emergency Shelter (Sheriff's Office)
listings.description: Nights, weekends and holidays: call the Sheriff's Office (or your local police) to get emergency shelter. Families with children should call here.
listings.hours_text: Nights, weekends and holidays (when Social Services is closed)
listings.notes: County Code Blue page: after hours, weekends and holidays call the Sheriff at (716) 753-4232 or a Code Blue authorizing agency. A 2024 county news release says families seeking shelter should call the Sheriff or nearest police.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: ROME Code Blue Overnight Warming Center
listings.description: Free warm place to sleep on Code Blue nights (32°F or colder, including wind chill). Open to anyone in need.
listings.hours_text: Code Blue nights only, 5:30 PM - 7:30 AM, Nov 1 - Apr 30
listings.schedule_note: Opens only on nights the county declares Code Blue (32°F or below incl. wind chill), Nov 1 through Apr 30. Text CODEBLUECHQ to 898211 for alerts.
listings.eligibility: County page: Code Blue provides shelter access to anyone in need. A 2024 county release says no referral is required and it is for individuals without minor children.
listings.notes: Run by Recovery Options Made Easy (ROME); ROME office is 560 W. 3rd St., Suite 23, Jamestown. A Nov 2024 Post-Journal article listed different phones (716-550-6657 for the center, 716-532-5508 for ROME); the county page lists 716-661-3845.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: UCAN City Mission
listings.description: Homeless shelter for men in Jamestown. Also an overnight Code Blue warming center on freezing nights.
listings.hours_text: Code Blue nights: 7:00 PM - 8:15 AM (referrals accepted at 9:00 PM while space lasts). Call for regular shelter intake.
listings.schedule_note: Code Blue warming hours apply only on declared Code Blue nights.
listings.eligibility: A 2024 Post-Journal article says the mission houses homeless males from Chautauqua County and guests are referred by DSS.
listings.notes: Men-only status is from an April 2024 news article (mission reopened then after a closure); confirm by phone.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: Code Blue Alerts by Text (211 WNY)

listings.hours_text: Alerts sent daily during Code Blue season
listings.notes: County page says daily alerts come through 211 WNY. The '211' phone value is the standard 2-1-1 dialing code, not listed on the page itself.
listings.source_name: Chautauqua County Code Blue page (official)

listings.name: Lifeline - Discounted or Free Phone Service
listings.description: Federal program that lowers the cost of phone or internet service for people with low income. Some plans end up free.
listings.hours_text: Support Center: every day 9 AM - 9 PM Eastern
listings.what_to_bring: Proof of income or proof you are in one of the programs.
listings.eligibility: Income at or below 135% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, OR you or someone in your household gets SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, or Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit.
listings.notes: FCC page lists the federal support as $9.25/month for broadband (voice-only support lower). Lifeline Support Center email: LifelineSupport@usac.org. Apply online through the Lifeline National Verifier or through a Lifeline phone company. Report fraud: 1-855-455-8477.
listings.source_name: Lifeline Support (USAC, official)

listings.name: Chemung County Mental Health Crisis Program (24/7)

listings.source_name: WETM MyTwinTiers, Dec 18 2025; Optum NY mobile crisis quick reference, Nov 2024

listings.name: Madison County Crisis Line (Liberty Resources Crisis Connects)

listings.notes: Madison County Helplines & Hotlines page lists 'Liberty Resources Crisis Services: 315-251-0800' and 'Madison County Mental Health Crisis Line: 315-366-2327' (the 366-2327 number is the county clinic's main line; 211 Lifeline shows its crisis line staffed only during clinic hours, M/W 8-6, Tu 8-8, Th/F 8-5). Optum NY mobile crisis list (Nov 2024) lists Liberty Resources Mobile Crisis Team for Madison at 1-855-778-1900, 24/7 - alternate number. 988 also works.
listings.source_name: Madison County government website; Optum NY mobile crisis list Nov 2024

listings.name: Wyoming County Crisis Line (24/7)
listings.description: 24/7 mental health crisis line for Wyoming County. Call any time for help in a mental health crisis; the team can come out to you.
listings.notes: Wyoming County Mental Health Dept. page and the county's Behavioral Health Resource Guide both list 'Wyoming County Crisis Line (585) 283-5200, 24/7'. Optum NY mobile crisis list (Nov 2024) shows the same number for the Rochester Psychiatric Center mobile integrated team serving Wyoming. The old listing's 888-448-3367 (ARA/Clarity) was not on any county page; it may only serve that clinic's own clients. 988 also works.
listings.source_name: Wyoming County government website

listings.name: Cortland County Mobile Crisis (Liberty Resources)
listings.description: Mobile crisis team for Cortland County, run by Liberty Resources. Call in a mental health crisis for phone help or to have a team come to you.
listings.hours_text: 24 hours, 7 days (per Nov 2024 list; local school page shows evenings/weekends only - see notes)
listings.notes: Optum NY mobile crisis quick reference (Nov 2024) lists Liberty Resources Mobile Crisis Team, 1-855-778-1900, 24/7, for Cortland. Onondaga County crisis page confirms 855-778-1900 is a Liberty Resources line. The old number 607-756-3771 is Guthrie Cortland Medical Center's main line: McGraw school counseling page says 'Cortland County Mobile Crisis Team: call Cortland Regional Medical Center (Guthrie) at 607-756-3771 or 911', with hours 'Mon-Fri 5pm-midnight, weekends and holidays 6am-midnight' (unclear which service). During business hours Cortland County Mental Health, 607-758-6100 (7 Clayton Ave), also takes crisis calls per Cortland Free Library page. SUNY Cortland lists 607-272-1616 (Suicide Prevention & Crisis Service, Ithaca) as a 24-hour line. 988 always works.
listings.source_name: Optum Behavioral Health NY mobile crisis quick reference, Nov 2024; McGraw CSD and Cortland Free Library pages

listings.notes: Mexico CSD page (Jan 2021) lists 'Oswego Health/Liberty Resources Mobile Crisis Team': Oswego Health Mobile Crisis 315-236-3500 (8am-5pm) and Crisis Connect Line 315-251-0800 (after 5pm). Optum NY list (Nov 2024) names 'Oswego Health Mobile Crisis Service' 24/7 with a different number (315-326-4100) - unconfirmed, not used. listings.name: NY Attorney General Abortion Legal Hotline (free lawyer callback)
listings.description: Free legal help about abortion rights in New York. Leave a message any time with just a phone number (no name needed) and a volunteer lawyer calls you back with know-your-rights info, legal guidance and referrals. Translation in 12 languages including Spanish.
listings.hours_text: Call any time; a lawyer calls you back
listings.eligibility: NY residents, anyone coming to NY for an abortion, people helping them (money, rides, lodging), and NY health care providers

listings.name: HEAP heating and cooling help (NYC)
listings.description: Help paying heat or electric bills. Emergency help if your heat or power is shut off or you are low on fuel. Apply online at ACCESS HRA, call 718-557-1399, or visit a HEAP office.
listings.schedule_note: Seasonal. As of the page: Regular HEAP 2025-26 closed Apr 10, 2026; Emergency HEAP closed Apr 24, 2026; HERR and Clean and Tune opened Oct 1, 2026. New regular/emergency season dates not yet posted.
listings.eligibility: Based on income or getting SNAP, cash assistance or certain SSI. Emergency HEAP needs a shutoff notice or low fuel, bill in your name, resources under $2,500 (under $3,750 if someone is 60+ or under 6).
listings.notes: Mail: HEAP, P.O. Box 1401, Church Street Station, New York, NY 10008. Fax 917-639-2900. In-person HEAP offices: Crotona (Bronx), Coney Island (Brooklyn), Lower Manhattan, Queens (LIC), Richmond (Staten Island) BACs, Mon-Fri 8:30-5.
listings.source_name: NYC HRA - Energy Assistance

listings.notes: From SNI program page; hours not listed. A 2026 application form is linked from the page. FDPIR cannot be used in the same month as SNAP (federal rule).

listings.name: Code Blue Buffalo (cold-weather emergency shelter)
listings.description: When it is 32°F or colder (temperature or wind chill), Code Blue opens overnight emergency shelter for anyone without a safe place to sleep, plus a daytime warming center 8am-8pm on cold days. Call 211 to find out if Code Blue is on tonight and where to go; outreach and transportation are part of the program.
listings.hours_text: Only on nights 32°F or colder; day warming center 8am-8pm on cold days
listings.schedule_note: Winter season only; Code Blue is called day by day and announced through 211.
listings.eligibility: Any man or woman experiencing homelessness or a housing emergency on a Code Blue night
listings.notes: Erie County press release (Nov 14, 2025) for 2025-26 season: Buffalo City Mission at 100 E. Tupper St. is the overnight Code Blue shelter and day warming center (8am-8pm); funded by Erie County, City of Buffalo, National Fuel; partners 211 WNY, Salvation Army, NFTA, Buffalo Police. Earlier WGRZ coverage (undated) listed other sites (Lincoln Field House 10 Quincy St; Holy Cross 412 Niagara St, men) and said outreach teams can be requested through 211 from 7-11pm and bus tickets to shelter are given at the NFTA Metro Transportation Center 6-9pm - these may vary by year, so call 211. Southern Erie County has its own Code Blue (see Rural Outreach Center).
listings.source_name: Erie County Executive press release, Nov 14 2025; WGRZ Code Blue article

listings.name: Western New York Law Center - Eviction Prevention Hotline
listings.description: Free legal help for low-income tenants facing eviction in Erie County (and Niagara, Wyoming, Orleans, Genesee). Call the hotline or apply online; Buffalo tenants can also ask for a lawyer at their first Buffalo City Court date.
listings.eligibility: Low-income tenants
listings.notes: From WNYLC Eviction Prevention page (c. 2025). Advice & Counsel line 716-828-8456; email evictions@wnylc.net. Part of WNY Eviction Prevention Project with NLS, Legal Aid Bureau, CELJ, ECBA VLP, UB Law, 211 WNY. No address on page.
listings.source_name: Western New York Law Center

listings.name: Legal Aid Bureau of Buffalo
listings.description: Free civil legal help including eviction defense for tenants in Buffalo City Court and Amherst and Cheektowaga town courts.
listings.eligibility: Low-income residents
listings.notes: From 8th Judicial District eviction provider list (COVID-era, undated): phone (716) 853-9555 x453 for evictions. Confirmed as current WNY-EPP partner on WNYLC page (2025).
listings.source_name: NYS Courts 8th Judicial District - Eviction civil legal service providers list (undated, COVID-era ~2020-21)

also.reentry: Can help with sealing records (NY Clean Slate).

listings.name: Center for Elder Law & Justice
listings.description: Free civil legal help for older adults, people with disabilities and low-income people, including eviction defense in Erie County courts.
listings.notes: Address/phone match on 8th Judicial District eviction provider list and 2017 UB Law brochure; WNY-EPP partner per WNYLC (2025).
listings.source_name: NYS Courts 8th Judicial District - Eviction civil legal service providers list (undated, COVID-era ~2020-21)

listings.name: Erie County Bar Association Volunteer Lawyers Project
listings.description: Free help from volunteer lawyers for low-income people, including tenants in Buffalo and Lackawanna City Courts.
listings.notes: From 8th Judicial District list (COVID-era). A 2017 UB Law brochure listed 237 Main St Suite 1000 and 716-847-0662 - office likely moved; use 438 Main/828-8460.
listings.source_name: NYS Courts 8th Judicial District - Eviction civil legal service providers list (undated, COVID-era ~2020-21)

listings.name: VA Buffalo Medical Center (VA Western New York)
listings.description: VA hospital for enrolled veterans; same-day mental health help with or without an appointment, and services for homeless veterans. Enrollment office helps veterans sign up for care.
listings.notes: Address and 24/7 from VA location page; main 716-834-9200 / 800-532-8387 and eligibility/enrollment 716-862-8829 from VA WNY contact page. Veterans Crisis Line: 988 press 1.
listings.source_name: VA Western New York Healthcare System

listings.name: Buffalo Vet Center
listings.description: Free, confidential counseling for combat veterans, service members, MST survivors and families - PTSD, grief, readjustment. No VA enrollment or particular discharge needed; anyone in crisis seen same day.
listings.notes: VA page didn't show main local number; 877-927-8387 is the 24/7 Vet Center call center; outreach specialist 716-862-7350.
listings.source_name: VA - Buffalo Vet Center

listings.name: VA Regional Benefit Office - Buffalo
listings.description: Help with VA disability claims, GI Bill and education benefits, VA letters and direct deposit; some services walk-in, others by appointment. Veterans service organization reps on 6th floor.
listings.what_to_bring: Current photo ID
listings.notes: From VA page; local number not shown so national benefits line given.
listings.source_name: VA - Buffalo Regional Benefit Office

listings.name: NFTA Metro Bus & Rail
listings.description: Buffalo-Niagara bus and Metro Rail. $2 a ride, $5 day pass, $25 7-day pass; kids under 10 free. Fare capping on MetGo card or Token Transit app means rides are free after $5/day, $25/week or $75/month.
listings.hours_text: Call or check app for schedules
listings.notes: From NFTA Fare Info page (c. 2026). Passes sold at Metro Rail station machines, Metropolitan Transportation Center (181 Ellicott St), airport, retail partners, Token Transit/Transit app. Cash on bus = single ride only, no capping. TTY 711.
listings.source_name: NFTA-Metro Fare Info

listings.name: NFTA Metro Reduced Fare Card (half fare)
listings.description: Half-price fares ($1 a ride) for people 65+, people on Medicare, people with qualifying disabilities, and families in county Community Care child-care programs. Card costs $2; photos taken at the downtown transportation center.
listings.hours_text: Photo ID cards Mon-Fri 7am-5pm at Metropolitan Transportation Center
listings.what_to_bring: Completed Reduced Fare Application (disability applicants); proof of age/Medicare
listings.eligibility: 65+, Medicare card holders, qualifying disabilities (incl. SSI for serious mental illness), Erie/Niagara Community Care families
listings.notes: From NFTA Reduced Fares page. Card not valid on PAL. 'What to bring' partly assumed - page doesn't list documents.
listings.source_name: NFTA-Metro Reduced Fares

listings.name: NFTA PAL Paratransit (Paratransit Access Line)
listings.description: Door-to-door shared rides for people whose disability keeps them from using regular buses or rail. $3.50 on PAL MetGo card or $4 cash; book by 4pm the day before - no same-day trips.
listings.hours_text: Phone reservations daily 8am-8pm; PAL Direct online 24/7
listings.eligibility: Must apply and be approved as PAL-eligible due to disability
listings.notes: From PAL General Info and Fare pages. Customer service 716-855-7268. 10-trip pass $35, 20-trip $70; attendants and kids 9 and under free.
listings.source_name: NFTA-Metro PAL

listings.name: Medicaid Transportation - Medical Answering Services (Erie County)
listings.description: Free rides to medical appointments for Medicaid members with no other way to get there. Call at least 3 business days ahead, 7am-6pm weekdays, or book online.
listings.eligibility: Medicaid members; prior approval required
listings.notes: Phone conflict: GoBuffaloNiagara medical transportation page lists 1-800-651-7040 for Erie County Medicaid transportation; NYS eMedNY provider contact list (3/11/2024) lists 1-866-932-7740 for Erie, Niagara and Chautauqua - that may be a provider/general line. 3-business-day rule and hours from MAS ordering guidelines.
listings.source_name: GoBuffaloNiagara; eMedNY Transportation contact list 3/11/2024; MAS ordering guidelines

listings.name: Homeless Coordinated Entry (Central Library basement)
listings.description: The front door to Erie County's homeless housing system: get assessed and connected to shelter and housing programs. Located in the basement of the downtown Central Library.
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (7/2026), which lists 'Coordinated Entry: Central Library basement, 1 Lafayette Sq, 716-936-2761'. Operator (likely Homeless Alliance of WNY) and hours not stated. After 5pm call 211.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

also.cleanup: Has a free hygiene Community Pantry.

listings.name: Erie County DSS Homeless Unit & Emergency Services (158 Pearl St)
listings.description: Go here during business hours if you have nowhere to sleep: the county Homeless Team can place you in a shelter, hotel or motel. Emergency Services also helps with one-time crises (rent arrears, utility shutoffs). After 5pm, call 211.
listings.what_to_bring: ID and any proof of income you have
listings.notes: DSS Homelessness page: Homeless Team at 158 Pearl St 1st floor; after 5pm call 2-1-1 WNY 1-888-696-9211 and follow up next business day. Handbook (1/2026) gives Homeless Unit/Emergency Services 716-858-6265; main DSS line 716-858-8000 is on the existing Rath Building listing - this listing is for the Pearl St entrance/Homeless Unit specifically. 'What to bring' is a general suggestion, not stated by county.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS - Homelessness; ECDSS Informational Handbook 1/2026

listings.name: Erie County SNAP (Food Stamps) Call Center
listings.description: Apply for SNAP by phone, ask about your case, or get help with the application. You can also apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov or in person at 158 Pearl St.
listings.notes: ECDSS Informational Handbook (footer 1/2026): SNAP Call Center 716-858-7239, 8:30-4:30; in person 158 Pearl St 3rd floor M-F 8-4. Work Supports Guide (7/2026) says 158 Pearl St 1st floor. Spanish and language line available.
listings.source_name: ECDSS Informational Handbook (1/2026)

listings.name: NYS Department of Labor - Buffalo Career Center
listings.description: Free job search help: resume help, skills assessment, workshops, job placement, plus free computers/internet, phones, fax and copiers for job seekers.
listings.eligibility: Anyone looking for work; registration required
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (7/2026). Also 1-888-469-7365.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: Workforce Buffalo Downtown Career Center (Buffalo Employment & Training Center)
listings.description: American Job Center with career counseling, help paying for job training, and career readiness workshops. Open to anyone looking for work.
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026); guide's phone was cut off ('716-9845'), email betc@wd.org. Phone not found - left null. BETC naming inferred from betc@ email.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: Matt Urban Hope Center (work clothes, essentials & outreach)
listings.description: Free work clothing for adults and kids and a personal-essentials pantry (toiletries etc.) for people with limited income; also does homeless street outreach.
listings.eligibility: Limited income
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026): ext. 306. Matt Urban's 'Hope Gardens' housing was not found in sources checked.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: St. Luke's Mission of Mercy - Mission Mall & Baby Room
listings.description: Free gently used clothing, shoes, linens and household goods, plus a Baby Room with diapers, wipes and baby clothes. Call for hours.
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026). St. Luke's also offers shelter and meals (listed in guide under community shelters) - food is covered by another researcher.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: Harvest House Baby & Children's Ministry
listings.description: Free baby and kids' clothing, cribs, car seats, strollers and more for low-income families, by appointment with a referral slip.
listings.what_to_bring: Referral slip (renewed every 3 years)
listings.eligibility: Low-income families
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026), listed as '175 Jefferson'.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: BestSelf Behavioral Health - Homeless Services
listings.description: Homeless outreach and services to help people living on the street or in shelters get housing and mental health care.
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026): 716-884-0888 or 716-856-9711; outreach line 716-856-2587.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: Veterans One-Stop Center of WNY
listings.description: Free help for veterans and families with benefits, education, jobs, legal and financial issues, and housing.
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026).
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

listings.name: Neighbor for Neighbor Heat Fund (Salvation Army / Catholic Charities)
listings.description: Emergency help with heating bills for older adults, people with disabilities, or households with a recent medical emergency - often used when HEAP runs out.
listings.eligibility: Older adults, people with disabilities, or recent medical emergency
listings.notes: From Erie County DSS Work Supports Guide (7/2026): apply via Salvation Army 716-888-6230 or Catholic Charities 716-856-4494.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS Work Supports Resource Guide (B-5664, 7/2026)

also.clothes: Same phone as the Salvation Army Family Resource Center (1000 Main St), which also gives clothing, hygiene items and winter coats: Mon 9am-1pm, Wed 11am-2pm, Fri 9am-1pm.
also.cleanup: Same phone as the Salvation Army Family Resource Center (1000 Main St), which also gives clothing, hygiene items and winter coats: Mon 9am-1pm, Wed 11am-2pm, Fri 9am-1pm.

listings.name: Erie County Auto Bureau (DMV) - Downtown Buffalo
listings.description: DMV office for non-driver photo ID, licenses and registrations. Reservations cut wait times; call the appointment hotline if you don't have internet.
listings.what_to_bring: Proofs of identity per NYS DMV ID checklist
listings.notes: From Erie County Clerk Locations & Hours page. 716-858-8864 = appointment hotline; Clerk main 716-858-8785. Other branches: Depew/Cheektowaga 2122 George Urban Blvd; Tonawanda 2309 Eggert Rd (Sat 8-2); West Seneca 1088-B Union Rd (Sat 7-noon); Williamsville Eastern Hills Mall; Evans 6853 Erie Rd. Mobile DMV at Merriweather Library, 1324 Jefferson Ave, Mondays 10-3.
listings.source_name: Erie County Clerk - Auto Bureau Locations & Hours

listings.name: Erie County Auto Bureau (DMV) - Tonawanda (Saturday hours)
listings.description: DMV branch in Sheridan Plaza with Saturday hours - for non-driver ID, licenses and registrations.
listings.schedule_note: Closed Saturdays before Monday holidays
listings.notes: From Erie County Clerk Locations & Hours page; 716-858-8864 is the county appointment hotline (no branch phone published).
listings.source_name: Erie County Clerk - Auto Bureau Locations & Hours

listings.name: Erie County Child Care Assistance (Day Care Unit, Dept. of Social Services)
listings.description: Help paying for child care for low-income working families, teen parents in school/GED, and parents in approved training. You can apply by mail; parents pay a sliding-scale share.
listings.what_to_bring: Recent pay stubs (or employer letter), proof of address and household (lease), child support form, Child Care Questionnaire (B-3923)
listings.eligibility: Income at or below 85% of NY state median income; working, in school/training, or on Temporary Assistance
listings.notes: All details from Erie County DSS day care page. Application form is OCFS-6025.
listings.source_name: Erie County Dept. of Social Services - Day Care page

listings.name: Child Care Resource Network (find child care in Erie County)
listings.description: Free help finding licensed child care in Erie County and help understanding child care subsidy. Call for referrals.
listings.notes: Address 1000 Hertel Ave per NYS CCR&R directory (2021, posted 2024); Erie County DSS page prints '100 Hertel Avenue' (likely typo). Phone 716-877-6666 matches both sources. Older health dept list names it Child Care Coalition of the Niagara Frontier at 2635 Delaware Ave (outdated).
listings.source_name: NYS CCR&R Directory 2021 (Council on Children & Families) + Erie County DSS day care page

listings.name: Child Care Resource & Referral of Niagara (NiaCAP)
listings.description: Free help finding child care in Niagara County and information on help paying for care. Run by Niagara Community Action Program.
listings.notes: Address/phone from NYS CCR&R directory (2021) and NYS Health Dept Early Intervention appendix (both list 1521 Main St, 716-285-8572; toll-free 1-800-701-4KID). Website from directory; not opened.
listings.source_name: NYS CCR&R Directory 2021; NYS DOH EIP Appendix C

listings.name: Head Start / Early Head Start - Connections North (Chautauqua Opportunities)
listings.description: Free preschool (Head Start) and infant/toddler program (Early Head Start) with free meals for income-eligible families. Call to enroll.
listings.what_to_bring: Child's birth certificate and proof of income are usually needed (call to confirm)
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with young children
listings.notes: From HHS Head Start center data via FeedAM directory (not independently confirmed). Phone 716-366-8176 is also Chautauqua Opportunities' Dunkirk office line (existing as a shelter/heat listing).
listings.source_name: FeedAM directory (HHS Head Start center data)

also.family: Runs Head Start and the county's child care referral service (Child Care Council).

listings.name: Head Start - Central Avenue (Chautauqua Opportunities)
listings.description: Free Head Start preschool with free breakfast, lunch and snack for income-eligible families. Call to enroll.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children ages 3-5
listings.notes: From HHS Head Start center data via FeedAM (60 funded slots). 716-366-3333 is Chautauqua Opportunities' Dunkirk admin line (Yerico building, 17 W Courtney St also listed as Head Start site).
listings.source_name: FeedAM directory (HHS Head Start center data)

also.family: Runs Head Start and the county's child care referral service (Child Care Council).

listings.name: Cattaraugus & Wyoming Counties Project Head Start (Olean)
listings.description: Free Head Start and Early Head Start for income-eligible families in Cattaraugus County. Call the Olean center to enroll or find the nearest site.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with young children
listings.notes: NYS OCFS child care facility record: open, license 11/2023-10/2027. Program runs multiple Cattaraugus sites (per Schumer/Gillibrand press releases).
listings.source_name: NYS OCFS Child Care facility search

listings.name: Cattaraugus County Youth Bureau (runaway & homeless youth, independent living)
listings.description: County youth bureau runs the Runaway & Homeless Youth Program, weekly independent living skills classes for ages 14-19 (jobs, money, home management), and youth court.
listings.eligibility: Youth in Cattaraugus County; independent living classes ages 14-19
listings.notes: Phone from county Youth Bureau contact page; page doesn't name the office address — 303 Court St Little Valley is the County Center listed on the same page (uncertain). Page also lists national runaway line 1-800-RUNAWAY.
listings.source_name: Cattaraugus County Youth Bureau pages

listings.name: GLYS WNY (Gay & Lesbian Youth Services) Drop-In Center
listings.description: Free drop-in center, support groups and programs for LGBTQ+ youth (about ages 12-21) and their friends. Also a helpline for parents/caregivers of trans and non-binary youth (716-393-2606).
listings.hours_text: Drop-in afternoons; call or check website for current hours
listings.schedule_note: Hours change in summer (July-Aug) vs school year.
listings.eligibility: LGBTQ+ youth roughly 12-21 (sources differ: 12-21 per WKBW 2021; 14-21 per CAC of Niagara listing)
listings.notes: Hours conflict: CenterLink directory says Tue & Thu 3-6pm; Child Advocacy Center of Niagara listing says Sep-Jun Mon/Wed/Thu 2:30-7:30pm, Jul-Aug Tue/Thu noon-5pm. Left hours blank. Address from CAC of Niagara listing; phone from CenterLink LGBTQ center directory. Everything except special events is free (WKBW).
listings.source_name: CenterLink LGBTQ Community Center directory; CAC of Niagara service listing; WKBW 6/24/2021

listings.name: Erie County Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
listings.description: Paid summer jobs ($16.50/hr in 2026) for Erie County youth ages 14-20 from lower-income households, run by Erie County DSS with the Buffalo Urban League.
listings.schedule_note: 2026 program ran June 29-Aug 28; applications were due June 5, 2026. Expect 2027 applications in spring.
listings.what_to_bring: TANF Youth Services Application, Pre-Employment Interest Questionnaire, signed consent form; ages 14-17 bring original working papers to the interview
listings.eligibility: Erie County residents ages 14-20; household income under 200% of poverty (or household gets TANF, Medicaid, SNAP, HEAP or SSI)
listings.notes: From 2026 SYEP application coversheet PDF (dated 5/26/26). Apply in person or by mail to DSS Comprehensive Employment Division. Program depends on NYS funding.
listings.source_name: Erie County DSS - 2026 SYEP application coversheet

listings.name: Buffalo Mayor's Summer Youth Internship & Employment Program
listings.description: Six weeks of paid summer work plus job-readiness training for City of Buffalo youth ages 14-21 and college students. Apply online in late winter/spring.
listings.schedule_note: Applications opened about March 1 in 2026; 2025 deadline was mid-April. Watch for 2027 sign-ups in early spring.
listings.eligibility: City of Buffalo residents ages 14-21, plus college students
listings.notes: From Spectrum News 3/1/2026 article; WGRZ article on an earlier year mentions an April 15 deadline. No phone found; zip is City Hall's.
listings.source_name: Spectrum News Buffalo, March 1, 2026

listings.name: Toys for Tots - Buffalo (sign up through 2-1-1 WNY)
listings.description: Free holiday toys for children of income-eligible families in Buffalo and surrounding areas. Families register by calling 2-1-1 WNY.
listings.schedule_note: 2025 applications were taken Oct 1 - Dec 6; 2026 dates not posted yet as of Oct 11, 2026 — likely similar. Call 211 or 888-696-9211.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible parents/guardians
listings.notes: From Buffalo NY Toys for Tots page (2025 season info). 2-1-1 can also give agency application sites and hours.
listings.source_name: Marine Toys for Tots - Buffalo NY campaign page

listings.name: Toys for Tots - Chautauqua County (online application)
listings.description: Free holiday toys for children from birth through age 17 in Chautauqua County. Families apply online through the local Toys for Tots portal (no phone line).
listings.schedule_note: Application portal opened in early October in 2025; toy drive runs mid-Nov to mid-Dec. Check the site for 2026 dates.
listings.eligibility: Children infant-17 in Chautauqua County
listings.notes: Post-Journal Oct 2025 article + local T4T page (page says they can't readily return phone calls; email only).
listings.source_name: Toys for Tots Chautauqua County page; Post-Journal Oct 2025

listings.name: Nurse-Family Partnership (Catholic Health) - first-time moms
listings.description: Free home visits by a nurse for first-time moms from pregnancy until the child turns 2. Covers Erie and Niagara counties.
listings.eligibility: Pregnant with first child, under 28 weeks, WIC- or Medicaid-eligible, living in Erie or Niagara County
listings.notes: All from Catholic Health NFP page. Email NurseFamilyPartnership@chsbuffalo.org. Serves Niagara County too.
listings.source_name: Catholic Health System - Nurse-Family Partnership page

listings.name: Head Start / Early Head Start - Lighthouse Center (CAO of WNY)
listings.description: Free preschool and infant/toddler care with free meals for income-eligible families, run with the Community Action Organization of WNY. Call to enroll.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children under 5
listings.notes: From HHS Head Start center data via FeedAM (record date 5/11/2026). CAO also lists partner sites at YWCA 1005 Grant St (716-447-1494) and Lighthouse Medical Park 150 E North St (716-259-9833). CAO main office 45 Jewett Ave.
listings.source_name: FeedAM directory (HHS Head Start center data, 2026)

listings.name: Head Start / Early Head Start - YWCA Grant St (CAO of WNY)
listings.description: Free Head Start/Early Head Start child care and preschool with free meals for income-eligible families on Buffalo's West Side. Call to enroll.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children under 5
listings.notes: From HHS Head Start center data via FeedAM; 16 funded slots.
listings.source_name: FeedAM directory (HHS Head Start center data)

listings.name: Head Start / Early Head Start - DiFrancesco Center (Niagara Falls schools)
listings.description: Free Head Start and Early Head Start (ages 6 weeks to 4 years) with meals and family services, run by the Niagara Falls City School District. Apply at the district registration office.
listings.what_to_bring: Child's proof of birth, proof of family income, current physical and immunization records
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children 6 weeks - 4 years
listings.notes: From NFCSD recruitment flyer (posted Oct 2024). Applications at district registration office, 630 66th St, Niagara Falls 14304 (716-286-4211). Center phone 716-216-3880 per 2021 list. Second site: Community Education Center, 6040 Lindbergh Ave.
listings.source_name: Niagara Falls City School District Head Start flyer (Oct 2024)

listings.name: Lockport Head Start
listings.description: Free Head Start preschool for income-eligible families in the Lockport area. Call to enroll.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children 3-5
listings.notes: From 2021 Head Start/Early Head Start list (scanned, partly garbled — confirm number). Since 2021 CAO of WNY runs Head Start in Lockport, Newfane and North Tonawanda (Lockport Journal 9/18/2021). Lockport Early Head Start listed at 6255 Campbell Blvd (716-302-5100).
listings.source_name: Head Start & Early Head Start list 2021 (Erie County 'The Pulse')

listings.name: North Tonawanda Head Start / Early Head Start
listings.description: Free Head Start and Early Head Start for income-eligible families in North Tonawanda. Call to enroll.
listings.eligibility: Income-eligible families with children under 5
listings.notes: From 2021 Head Start list (scanned; confirm number). Operated by CAO of WNY since 2021 per Lockport Journal. Newfane site: 6048 Godfrey Rd, Burt (716-638-9100).
listings.source_name: Head Start & Early Head Start list 2021

listings.name: West Side Diaper Bank (West Side Community Services & Every Bottom Covered)
listings.description: Free diapers twice a month (up to 25 per pickup) for families on Buffalo's West Side, at Provisions 139.
listings.schedule_note: Two pickup windows a month: 1st-14th and 15th-end of month.
listings.what_to_bring: Photo ID, proof of address, children's birth certificates (at registration/first visit)
listings.eligibility: Residents of zip codes 14201, 14209, 14213, 14222
listings.notes: Only source is WKBW article from Nov 2022 (opening). No phone given; West Side Community Services food pantry (716-970-1325) is an existing listing — call there to confirm the diaper bank is still running.
listings.source_name: WKBW, Nov 15, 2022

listings.eligibility: Call to see if you qualify
listings.notes: Phone from county Office for the Aging guide (2023). Niagara County home-delivered meals for seniors also via NY Connects 716-438-3030.

listings.name: Community Missions - Emergency Shelter
listings.description: 24/7 emergency housing and crisis shelter. Also runs Falls Street Station shelter for ages 18-24 and a Youth Resource Hub at 1622 Falls St.
listings.hours_text: 24 hours - call and dial 0 for shelter information
listings.eligibility: Individuals and families; youth shelter ages 18-24
listings.notes: 24/7 and 'dial 0' from OMH guide (Dec 2025). Youth shelter and hub from county homeless services sheet (2023).
listings.source_name: NYS OMH Niagara County Resource Guide (revised Dec 2025); Niagara County Homeless Services sheet (file dated 5/1/2023)

listings.name: Niagara Gospel Rescue Mission - Men's Shelter
listings.description: Overnight emergency shelter for men with a shower, hygiene supplies, a meal and a safe, sober bed. Short stays (about 30 days). Also transitional rooms and a faith-based recovery program.
listings.hours_text: Open 365 days - call for check-in time
listings.eligibility: Adult men
listings.notes: From homelessshelterdirectory (updated Mar 2023) and county homeless services sheet (2023). Address conflict 1317 vs 317 Portage - see dining room listing.
listings.source_name: homelessshelterdirectory.org (Mar 2023); Niagara County Homeless Services sheet (file dated 5/1/2023)

also.clothes: Free 'Closing Closet': Tue and Thu 10am-2pm, up to 10 free items, open to anyone (2022 source).

listings.name: Lockport CARES Emergency Shelter
listings.description: Emergency shelter in Lockport for individuals and families.
listings.eligibility: Individuals and families
listings.notes: Listed on Niagara County homeless services sheet (2023). Address not published there; not otherwise verified.
listings.source_name: Niagara County Homeless Services sheet (file dated 5/1/2023)

listings.name: Homeless Help - Coordinated Entry (Heart, Love & Soul)
listings.description: If you are homeless or about to be, call to get on the list for housing programs in Niagara County.
listings.notes: Heart Love & Soul is the Coordinated Entry lead per county homeless services sheet (2023). Same phone as their pantry. After hours: Niagara County DSS emergency housing goes through Crisis Services 716-285-3515.
listings.source_name: Niagara County Homeless Services sheet (file dated 5/1/2023)

listings.name: Casey House Youth Shelter (Pinnacle Community Services)
listings.description: Emergency shelter for youth ages 12-17, with a 24/7 runaway youth hotline.
listings.eligibility: Ages 12-17
listings.notes: From county homeless services sheet (2023). Pinnacle's Family Engagement Team (ages 12-24) is at 1552 Main St, Niagara Falls, 716-285-6984.
listings.source_name: Niagara County Homeless Services sheet (file dated 5/1/2023)

listings.name: Community Health Center of Niagara Falls (CHCB)
listings.description: Low-cost primary care clinic. Sliding fees for people without insurance; takes Medicaid. STD/HIV testing and PrEP.

listings.notes: From CDC NPIN listing.

listings.name: Community Health Center of Lockport (CHCB)

listings.eligibility: Anyone; fees based on income

listings.name: Niagara County Health Dept - Sexual Health Center

listings.name: NFTA Metro buses (Niagara County)
listings.description: Metro buses in Niagara Falls, North Tonawanda and to Buffalo. $2 a ride; reduced fare for seniors 65+, people with disabilities, and Community Care members.
listings.notes: Route 59 serves Niagara Falls Airport / SUNY Niagara. Free transfers from Connect Niagara.
listings.source_name: NFTA Metro How to Ride guide

listings.name: Erie County Department for the Aging (NY Connects)
listings.description: County office for people 60+. One call for home-delivered meals assessment, HIICAP Medicare counseling, HEAP help, Going Places rides, case management and caregiver help.
listings.eligibility: Erie County residents 60+ and caregivers
listings.notes: Address, hours, phone and service list from Erie County Dept. for the Aging page. Senior Services line for dining-site info is 716-858-7639 per same page. Page lists email as senior.info@erie.gov but link goes to seniorinfo@erie.gov.
listings.source_name: Erie County Department for the Aging (page last changed Mar 2022; contact block current site template)

listings.name: Going Places Senior Van Service (Erie County)
listings.description: Van rides for people 60+ who can't use regular transportation: doctor visits, pharmacy, groceries, senior dining sites, bank, HEAP/legal appointments. Register first, then book.
listings.schedule_note: Book health trips 2 weeks ahead, other trips 1 week ahead. Van hours vary by town (Buffalo 8:30am-3:15pm).
listings.eligibility: Erie County residents 60+ who can't use conventional transportation
listings.notes: Phone is 716-858-RIDE. Suggested donation $8 each way; no one denied. Wheelchair vans may be available on request.
listings.source_name: Erie County Department for the Aging

listings.name: Erie County Adult Protective Services (report elder abuse)
listings.description: Report abuse, neglect or money exploitation of an older or disabled adult living in the community. For abuse in a nursing home or facility, call the NYS Justice Center at 518-549-0200.
listings.notes: Page gives no hours or after-hours number for APS; in immediate danger call 911. Statewide hotline 1-855-373-2122 also listed on same page.
