listings.notes: From Livingston County transportation guide (undated): phones 585-593-1738 or 585-593-5223; fares not listed - call. FTA profile: Allegany County (7 Court St, Belmont) runs bus service, 49,258 trips in 2024. Allegany legislature voted Oct 2024 to merge with Cattaraugus County's system (WLEA).
listings.source_name: Livingston County transportation resource guide (undated)

hotlines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone in emotional distress, suicidal crisis, or worried about someone else
hotlines.call_note: Press 1 for Veterans Crisis Line; press 2 for Spanish; press 3 for LGBTQ+ youth (restored Sept 30, 2026)
hotlines.text_keyword: Any message in English; text AYUDA to 988 for Spanish
hotlines.other: Deaf/hard of hearing: call 988 from a videophone (988 Videophone, ASL, 24/7). TTY: use your relay service or dial 711 then 988.
hotlines.notes: The LGBTQ+ youth 'Press 3' option ended July 17, 2025 and was restored Sept 30, 2026. 988lifeline.org/faq says it 'has been restored.' Confirmed only for calls. The site and news reports do not say whether text or chat (the old 'text PRIDE') came back. The operator was not named, and news reports say The Trevor Project is not running it. HHS did not rule out removing it again. Other sources: 988lifeline.org/faq/, 988lifeline.org/faq/calling-the-988-lifeline/, 988lifeline.org/deaf-hard-of-hearing-hearing-loss/. Interpretation exists but the language count was not stated.

hotlines.name: Veterans Crisis Line
hotlines.for_whom: Veterans, service members (including Guard and Reserve), and their families and friends; no VA enrollment needed
hotlines.other: Overseas: Europe 844-702-5495, Indo-Pacific 844-702-5493, Central 855-422-7719, Africa 888-482-6054, Southern 866-989-9599 (or DSN 988)
hotlines.notes: Confirmed on militaryonesource.mil and va.gov (VA news release). Also confirmed on 988lifeline.org/get-help: 'Text 838255', press 1. The fetch tool could not load veteranscrisisline.net directly. A TTY/deaf-specific option was not confirmed (988 Videophone and 711 relay are available through 988). Languages were not stated.

hotlines.name: Crisis Text Line
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone in any kind of crisis who prefers texting
hotlines.other: WhatsApp: message +1 443-787-7678 with the word CONNECT
hotlines.notes: An older 2021 blog post says Spanish users can also text AYUDA to 741741 or WhatsApp 442-AYUDAME. The current About page lists HOLA instead, so the Spanish WhatsApp option is not confirmed as current and is left out.

hotlines.name: The Trevor Project
hotlines.notes: Trevor's own services were not affected when 988 'Press 3' ended in July 2025, and Trevor is reportedly not running the restored Press 3 line. An age limit was not stated on the get-help page (the July 2025 statement refers to youth under 25). Chat is the 'Start Chat' button on that page. Languages were not stated.

hotlines.name: Trans Lifeline
hotlines.for_whom: Trans and questioning people; peer support run by trans people; you don't need to be in crisis
hotlines.notes: Limited hours. For a crisis outside those hours, use 988 or Trevor.

hotlines.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone experiencing domestic violence or abuse, or worried about someone
hotlines.other: Deaf Hotline videophone: 1-855-812-1001. Spanish site: espanol.thehotline.org
hotlines.notes: The 24/7 hours are confirmed on espanol.thehotline.org. Chat is the 'Chat live now' button on thehotline.org; no separate chat URL was shown. The old TTY number (1-800-787-3224) is no longer listed on the site. Deaf services are now shown as the Deaf Hotline videophone 855-812-1001 (thehotline.org/resources/abuse-in-deaf-communities/), so the TTY is not included. The site also has an AI chat (ruth.thehotline.org), which is not a human advocate. It warns of long wait times.

hotlines.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
hotlines.for_whom: Native Americans and Alaska Natives facing domestic, dating, or sexual violence
hotlines.notes: Chat is the chat icon on the get-help page; chat is not offered to people under 13, but phone is open to all ages. After texting, replies come from a secondary number. Languages were not stated.

hotlines.name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
hotlines.for_whom: Survivors of sexual assault or abuse and their loved ones
hotlines.notes: A text option (HOPE to 64673) is now listed. Older materials list only phone and online chat (previously hotline.rainn.org/online); the current chat link is RAINN.org/hotline. Also confirmed on rainn.org/support.

hotlines.name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
hotlines.for_whom: People who are pregnant or just had a baby, and new parents (and their families)
hotlines.notes: Run by HRSA. The site says call or text; web chat is also listed. TTY was not mentioned.

hotlines.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
hotlines.for_whom: People and families facing mental health or substance use problems; free treatment referral and information (not a crisis counseling line)
hotlines.notes: Free and confidential. The page does not mention a text option (e.g., 435748) or a TTY, so those are not included. For a crisis, the page points to 988.

hotlines.name: NAMI HelpLine
hotlines.for_whom: People with mental health conditions, families and caregivers seeking information, support, and resources (not a crisis line)
hotlines.notes: Chat is offered on nami.org but no direct URL was confirmed. For a crisis, NAMI directs people to call or text 988. Languages were not stated.

hotlines.for_whom: Anyone needing local help: food, housing, utilities, bills, healthcare, mental health, substance use, disaster recovery
hotlines.other: Website search by address, ZIP, or county: https://www.211.org
hotlines.languages: English, Spanish (site); other languages vary by local 211
hotlines.notes: Texting is offered by some local 211s and is not national, so none is listed.

hotlines.name: Poison Help line (Poison Control)
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone with a possible poisoning, or questions about poison risks
hotlines.languages: Interpretation in 161 languages (an image caption says 'over 100')
hotlines.notes: Free and confidential; works from anywhere in the U.S. and many territories. Text and chat were not mentioned on the HRSA page. Call 911 if the person is unconscious, not breathing, or having a seizure.

hotlines.name: National Runaway Safeline
hotlines.for_whom: Youth about 12-24 who are thinking of running away, have run away, or are homeless or in crisis, and their families
hotlines.other: Email form and a (not real-time) forum on the site
hotlines.notes: The age range 12-24 comes from the site's page description. Chat is the 'Chat live now' link on the get-help page (opens an iCarol chat). Languages were not stated.

hotlines.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
hotlines.for_whom: Children, parents, and anyone worried about child abuse (U.S. and Canada)
hotlines.languages: Over 170 languages via interpreters; Spanish spoken
hotlines.notes: Text GO to 800.422.4453 (childhelphotline.org/text/). The site has a 'Click To Live Chat' button but no direct chat URL. Hours and languages were confirmed on the childhelphotline.org main page.

hotlines.name: findhelp.org
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone looking for free or reduced-cost local programs (food, housing, transportation, bills, health)
hotlines.other: Free website: enter a ZIP code to browse programs by category and eligibility
hotlines.notes: The fetch tool could not load findhelp.org itself. The description was confirmed only through a partner (UAB Medicine) page, which links to a co-branded findhelp.com site. The URL https://www.findhelp.org is widely cited (formerly Aunt Bertha) but was not opened directly. Verify by hand before shipping.

hotlines.name: Lifeline (FCC free/discount phone and internet)
hotlines.for_whom: Households with income at or below 135% of federal poverty guidelines, or on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, or Veterans Pension (extra Tribal programs on Tribal lands); one per household
hotlines.call_note: Lifeline Support Center (USAC), for questions and applications, not crisis
hotlines.other: Apply: https://www.lifelinesupport.org (National Verifier) or through a participating phone company
hotlines.notes: Benefit: up to $9.25/month (up to $34.25 on Tribal lands). Since Sept 2024, survivors of domestic violence and trafficking with financial hardship can get emergency Lifeline for up to 6 months (FCC fact sheet, reviewed Nov 2024). California, Texas, and Oregon use state processes. Support center hours were not stated.

hotlines.name: All-Options Talkline
hotlines.for_whom: Anyone pregnant or who has been pregnant, and their partners, family, and friends; judgment-free support on abortion, adoption, parenting, pregnancy loss, infertility
hotlines.call_note: If you get voicemail, leave first name, number, and time zone; callback within 48 hours
hotlines.notes: The page presents it as active (no closure notice) and it serves the U.S. and Canada. Hours and languages were not listed (flyers are in English and Spanish). It is staffed by volunteer peer counselors, not a crisis line; for crisis the page points to 988.

howto.title: How to apply for SNAP (food stamps) in Chautauqua County
steps: Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov - or call 716-661-8200 (Jamestown) or 716-363-3500 (Dunkirk) to get a paper form mailed, or pick one up at either office.
You can turn in the form the same day with just your name, address (if you have one) and signature. Add a phone number if you can.
Turn it in online, by mail, in person, or by fax to 716-661-8225.
Do the interview by phone or in person - you choose. If you have very little money or food, ask about expedited SNAP (can come within 5 days).
Send proof they ask for: ID, Social Security numbers, rent or mortgage, pay stubs and other income, child care and medical costs.
You will get a decision within 30 days. Benefits count from the day you applied.
Need help with the form? Call NOEP at 716-244-7337 or 877-686-9209.

howto.title: How to apply for HEAP (help with heating bills)
steps: Check the season: in 2025-26 Regular HEAP ran Dec 1 to Apr 7 and Emergency HEAP from Jan 2. New season dates are announced by the state each fall.
Regular HEAP: apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov (fastest), or call 716-661-8103 to have a paper form mailed to you.
Mail the form to HEAP Office, 110 East 4th Street, Jamestown, NY 14701, or drop it at 110 E. 4th St, Jamestown or 15 W. Lucas Ave, Dunkirk.
Sign the Consent and Signature section of the application.
Interviews are done by phone - you don't have to go to an office.
Shutoff notice or almost out of fuel? Call 716-661-8103 for Emergency HEAP. It can't be done online.
Already on SNAP or cash assistance? Call your worker about HEAP.
Questions: state HEAP hotline 1-800-342-3009.

howto.title: How to get a copy of your NY birth certificate (born outside NYC)
steps: You can order your own, or your child's if you are a parent named on it. Others need a court order.
Get your ID ready: driver license, non-driver photo ID, US passport, or military photo ID. No photo ID? Use two of: utility bills, phone bills, or a government letter from the last 6 months.
Fastest locally: go to the city or town clerk where you were born. Jamestown City Clerk, 200 E. Third St (716-483-7612), $30 - in person can be same day.
Or order from New York State online or by phone through VitalChek (1-877-854-4481): $45 per copy plus an $8 fee.
Or mail form DOH-4380 with a check or money order ($30, no cash) to NYS Dept. of Health, Vital Records Certification Unit, P.O. Box 2602, Albany, NY 12220-2602.
State questions: 855-322-1022, Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm.

howto.title: How to get a New York non-driver ID
steps: Use the NY DMV online pre-screening tool to see which documents you need (full list on form ID-44).
Fill out form MV-44 (or print the application from the pre-screening tool).
Gather your proofs of identity, proof of date of birth, and your Social Security card (or proof you are not eligible for one).
Go in person to a DMV office - you cannot apply online. In Chautauqua County: Jamestown, Dunkirk or Mayville (book at the county's appointment links). Arrive by 3:15pm for new IDs.
Pay the fee. (Replacing a lost license or ID costs $17.50 at the county DMV.)
You get a paper temporary ID that day, good for 60 days. Your card comes in the mail.
Under 21 or applying for a child under 16: a parent fills out form MV-45 in person at the DMV.

howto.title: How to replace a Social Security card
steps: First ask yourself if you really need the card - often knowing your number is enough.
The card is free. Never pay a website to get one.
Start online at ssa.gov/number-card/replace-card - it's the fastest way, if your situation allows it.
If you can't do it online, call 1-800-772-1213 (Mon-Fri 8am-7pm; TTY 1-800-325-0778) or make an appointment at the Dunkirk office, 437 Main St, Suite 2 (888-862-2139).
The office cannot print a card on the spot. Your card comes by mail in 5-10 business days after your request is done.

howto.title: How to apply for SNAP (food stamps) in Erie County
steps: Apply online any time at mybenefits.ny.gov - it's the fastest way to get your application date on file.
Or apply by phone: call the Erie County SNAP Call Center at 716-858-7239 (Mon-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm). Spanish speakers and interpreters are available.
Or apply in person at Erie County DSS, 158 Pearl St, Buffalo (Mon-Fri 8am-4pm). Metro Rail and many bus routes stop nearby downtown.
If you have almost no money (under $100 in cash/bank) or very low income, ask for EXPEDITED SNAP - eligible households can get benefits within 5 days.
You'll have an interview (usually by phone). Have ID, proof of income (pay stubs), rent and utility bills ready; they'll tell you anything else to send.
If you already get Temporary Assistance (cash), you don't need a separate SNAP application.
Benefits come on an EBT card you use like a debit card at grocery stores.

howto.title: Nowhere to sleep tonight in Erie County - what to do
steps: If you're in danger or need medical help, call 911.

Weekdays during business hours: go to the Erie County DSS Homeless Team, 158 Pearl St, 1st floor, Buffalo. They can place you in a shelter, hotel or motel. Phone 716-858-6265 (main DSS line 716-858-8000).
After 5pm, weekends and holidays: call 2-1-1 (or 1-888-696-9211). 211 WNY can find you a place to stay tonight. Go back to the Homeless Team at 158 Pearl St the next business day.

Men can go to the Buffalo City Mission, 100 E Tupper St - intake is open 24/7 (716-854-8181). Women and women with children: Buffalo City Mission's Cornerstone Manor, intake 24/7 - call 716-854-8181 ext. 111.
Youth 12-17 (or young people in trouble): Compass House 24-hour crisis line 716-886-0935.
Fleeing domestic violence: call the Haven House 24-hour hotline 716-884-6000 for a confidential safe shelter.

When it's 32°F or colder, Code Blue is on: the Buffalo City Mission takes anyone overnight and runs a day warming center 8am-8pm. Call 211 to check, or text CodeBlueBuffalo to 898-211 (Southern Erie: text CodeBlueSouthernErie).
To get on the list for longer-term housing, contact Coordinated Entry (Central Library basement, 1 Lafayette Square) at 716-936-2761.

howto.title: How to get HEAP heating help in Erie County
steps: HEAP helps pay heating bills (and sometimes cooling). The season usually runs about November to May - call to check when it opens this year.
Regular HEAP: call the Erie County HEAP hotline at 716-858-7644 or the HEAP application line 716-858-1969, or apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov.
If you get SNAP or Temporary Assistance, you may get a basic HEAP benefit automatically.

EMERGENCY HEAP (shut-off notice, no heat, or almost out of fuel): you must apply in person at Erie County HEAP, 460 Main St, 2nd floor, Buffalo. Bring your shut-off notice or fuel bill, ID, and proof of income.
After the HEAP season ends (about mid-May), utility emergencies go to the DSS Emergency Services Unit, 158 Pearl St (4th floor), 716-858-6265.

If HEAP is used up: older adults, people with disabilities, or households with a recent medical emergency can ask about the Neighbor for Neighbor Heat Fund - Salvation Army 716-888-6230 or Catholic Charities 716-856-4494.
For free weatherization (insulation, furnace help) call Neighborhood Housing Services of South Buffalo 716-823-3630 x102 or Supportive Services Corp 716-685-6252.

howto.title: How to apply for Medicaid (free health insurance) in Erie County
steps: Most adults, kids and pregnant people apply through NY State of Health: online at nystateofhealth.ny.gov or by phone at 1-855-355-5777.
Or ask for a paper application from Erie County DSS Medicaid: call 716-858-6244 or pick one up at 158 Pearl St, Buffalo. Face-to-face interviews are optional.
People 65+, people on Medicare, and people needing long-term care may need to apply through the county instead - call 716-858-6244 to ask.
Pregnant? You can get prenatal care right away through the Prenatal Care Assistance Program - call the Growing Up Healthy Hotline 1-800-522-5006.

Free help applying: community health centers like Jericho Road (716-881-6191), Neighborhood Health Center, and Community Health Center of Buffalo (716-986-9199) have staff who help uninsured patients sign up.
While you wait, community health centers will see you on a sliding fee based on income.

howto.title: How to apply for SNAP (food stamps) in Niagara County
steps: Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov - it's the fastest way.
Or apply in person at the Niagara Falls DSS office, 301 10th Street (corner of 10th and Falls St), Niagara Falls. Walk-in hours Mon-Fri 8:00am-3:45pm.
Questions or want a paper form? Call 716-278-8400 (phones 8am-4pm).
You can hand in the form with just your name, address and signature - that saves your start date.
Do your interview (phone or in person). If you have almost no money or food, ask for expedited SNAP - it can come within days.
Bring or send proof: photo ID, Social Security numbers, pay stubs or other income, rent and utility bills.
Need help filling it out? FeedMore WNY SNAP outreach: 716-822-2005 ext. 3035.

howto.title: Need a place to stay tonight in Niagara County
steps: Daytime (Mon-Fri 8am-3:45pm): go to Niagara County DSS, 301 10th Street, Niagara Falls, or 20 East Avenue, Lockport, and ask for emergency housing. Phone 716-278-8400.
Nights, weekends and holidays: call Niagara County Crisis Services at 716-285-3515 - they handle after-hours emergency housing for DSS.
Community Missions emergency shelter, 1570 Buffalo Ave, Niagara Falls is open 24/7: call 716-285-3403 and dial 0. Ages 18-24 can ask about their Falls Street Station youth shelter.
Men can also call Niagara Gospel Rescue Mission, Niagara Falls: 716-205-8805 (open every night; free dinner daily at 6pm).
In Lockport, call Lockport CARES: 716-438-2273.
Under 18? Call Casey House youth shelter / runaway line 24/7: 716-285-7125.
Unsafe at home? YWCA hotline 716-433-6716 (call or text) or Passage House 716-299-0909, both 24/7.
To get on the list for longer-term housing, call Coordinated Entry at Heart, Love & Soul: 716-282-5687.

howto.title: How to get help with heating bills (HEAP) in Niagara County
steps: 2026-27 dates: Regular HEAP opens November 2, 2026. Heating repair/replacement and Clean & Tune opened October 1, 2026. Emergency HEAP opens later in winter.
Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov, or in person at DSS: 20 East Avenue, Lockport or 301 10th Street, Niagara Falls (Mon-Fri 8:00am-3:45pm).
Call the HEAP office with questions: 716-278-8400.
Age 60+ or disabled? The Office for the Aging takes your HEAP application: 716-438-4020.
Already on SNAP? Call your SNAP worker about HEAP instead of applying again.
Got a shut-off notice or almost out of fuel? Call 716-278-8400 for Emergency HEAP once it opens.
Ask NiaCAP about free weatherization: 716-285-9681.

howto.title: How to apply for Medicaid in Niagara County
steps: Most adults under 65 and families apply through NY State of Health: nystateofhealth.ny.gov or 1-855-355-5777.
If you are 65+, blind, or disabled (or need long-term care), apply with Niagara County DSS at the Lockport office, 20 East Avenue, Lockport (across from the library). Walk-in Mon-Fri 8:00am-3:45pm.
Call DSS with questions: 716-278-8400.
Bring ID, proof of address, proof of income, and any insurance cards.
Need a ride to a doctor once you have Medicaid? Call Medical Answering Services: 1-866-753-4543.
Low-cost care while you wait: Community Health Center in Niagara Falls (2715 Highland Ave) or Lockport (100 Main St), 716-986-9199 - sliding fees.

howto.title: How to apply for SNAP (food stamps) in Cattaraugus County
steps: Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov, or get a paper application from Cattaraugus County DSS, 1 Leo Moss Drive, Suite 600, Olean, NY 14760 (phone 716-373-8065, Mon-Fri 8:30am-4pm).
You can turn in the form the same day with just your name, address (if you have one) and signature - this sets your start date.
Turn it in online, by mail, or in person at the Olean office. Call 716-373-8065 first if you are unsure where to go.
Do the interview (usually by phone). If you have almost no money or food, ask for expedited SNAP - it can come within 5 days.
Send the proof they ask for: ID, Social Security numbers, rent, pay stubs or other income, child care and medical costs.
You should get a decision within 30 days. Need food now? Call the Olean Food Pantry 716-372-4989 or Cattaraugus Community Action 716-945-1041, or dial 211.

howto.title: Nowhere to sleep tonight in Cattaraugus County
steps: Weekdays during business hours: go to or call Cattaraugus County DSS, 1 Leo Moss Drive, Suite 600, Olean (716-373-8065) and say you are homeless and need emergency housing today.
Nights, weekends and holidays: call 716-938-9111 (Sheriff's dispatch) and ask for the DSS after-hours emergency worker.
Genesis House of Olean (107 S. Barry St., 716-373-3354) runs shelters for families and single adults and is the county's Code Blue hub with a winter warming center.
In freezing weather (Code Blue), shelters must take people in - ask DSS or Genesis House where to go.
If you are fleeing abuse, call the CCA 24-hour hotline 1-888-945-3970 for a safe, confidential shelter.
You can also dial 211 any time for help finding a bed.

howto.title: How to get HEAP heating help in Cattaraugus County
steps: HEAP helps pay for heat (gas, electric, oil, propane, wood, etc.). Regular HEAP usually opens in the fall (often November).
Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov or through Cattaraugus County DSS HEAP, 1 Leo Moss Drive, Suite 6010, Olean, NY 14760, phone 716-701-3518.
Have ready: ID, Social Security numbers for everyone in the home, proof of income for the last month, and a recent heating and electric bill.
If your heat is shut off, you are almost out of fuel, or you have a shut-off notice, ask for Emergency HEAP - call DSS right away (716-373-8065).
After hours with no heat in dangerous cold, call 716-938-9111 and ask for the DSS emergency worker.

howto.title: How to apply for SNAP (food stamps) in Allegany County
steps: Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov, or get a paper application from Allegany County DSS in Belmont (phone 585-268-9622).
You can turn in the form the same day with just your name, address (if you have one) and signature - this sets your start date.
Turn it in online, by mail, or in person at DSS in Belmont. Call 585-268-9622 if you need the form mailed to you.
Do the interview (usually by phone). If you have almost no money or food, ask for expedited SNAP - it can come within 5 days.
Send proof they ask for: ID, Social Security numbers, rent, pay stubs or other income, child care and medical costs.
Need food now? ACCORD Food Pantry, 84 Schuyler St, Belmont (585-268-7605), or the Salvation Army, 25 E Pearl St, Wellsville (585-593-2640). Or dial 211.

howto.title: Nowhere to sleep tonight in Allegany County
steps: Weekdays during business hours: call or go to Allegany County DSS in Belmont (585-268-9622) and say you are homeless and need emergency housing today.
Nights, weekends and holidays: call the DSS after-hours line 585-268-9189.
In freezing weather (Code Blue), DSS must find you a warm place - tell them it's an emergency.
If you are fleeing abuse, call ACCORD's 24-hour domestic violence hotline 1-800-593-5322 for a safe, confidential shelter.
You can also dial 211 any time for help.

howto.title: How to get HEAP heating help in Allegany County
steps: HEAP helps pay for heat (gas, electric, oil, propane, wood, etc.). Regular HEAP usually opens in the fall (often November).
Apply online at mybenefits.ny.gov or through Allegany County DSS HEAP, 7 Court Street, Belmont, NY 14813, phone 585-268-9326.
Have ready: ID, Social Security numbers for everyone in the home, proof of income for the last month, and a recent heating and electric bill.
If your heat is shut off, you are almost out of fuel, or you have a shut-off notice, ask for Emergency HEAP right away (585-268-9326 or 585-268-9622).
After hours with no heat in dangerous cold, call 585-268-9189 (DSS after-hours).

Chautauqua.agency: CHQ Transit (Chautauqua Area Regional Transit System, CARTS) - Chautauqua County
Chautauqua.phone: South County 716-665-6466; North County 716-366-4500; Toll free 800-388-6534
Chautauqua.fares: Zone-based (zones are townships). County fare chart (effective 1/1/2012, may be outdated): City/rural on-route one-way $2.25 (Zone 1) up to $4.75 (Zone 6); round trip $4.25-$8.50; 10-trip $16.75-$33.50; monthly $58.75-$117.25. Rural route off-route one-way $4.00-$6.50. Dial-A-Ride curb-to-curb one-way $6.00-$13.50; door-to-door $11.25-$26.25. Fixed routes sell one-way, 10-trip, monthly and all-day passes (no round trip on fixed routes, per SUNY Fredonia page). Cash or check only; drivers cannot make change. Children under 5 ride free with an adult.
Chautauqua.reduced_fares: Reduced fares for seniors 60+ (proof of age), riders with a CARTS Disabled Fare Card (application from the driver or online 'Disabled Fare Application for CHQ Transit'), and high school/college/K-12 students with valid ID. 2012 chart: reduced city/rural on-route one-way $1.75 (Zone 1) to $3.00 (Zone 6). ADA paratransit fares for ADA-certified riders - call 665-6466 to apply. No low-income or Medicare discount found.
Chautauqua.routes_summary: City buses in Jamestown (North Main, Southwest Express, Baker, Willard, Falconer routes), Jamestown-Lakewood (Jones & Gifford, Fairmount), Celoron, Falconer, and Dunkirk (Green and Red routes), plus Fredonia. Saturday city service in Jamestown and Dunkirk. Rural routes run countywide, linking Jamestown and Dunkirk to smaller towns (South-to-North County, Southwest, Routes 394/430, North, Northwest, East/Southeast County); rural riders must schedule ahead and the bus may go off-route. Summer Saturday tourism trolley routes. A Tuesday grocery run is mentioned (call 716-665-6466). Get the Schedule Book PDF on the Routes & Schedules page.
Chautauqua.demand_response: Dial-A-Ride (curb-to-curb or door-to-door) for people who cannot use fixed routes because of a disability; schedule in advance through the CHQ Transit office (as early as possible). Rural routes also require advance scheduling.

medicaid_rides.name: Medical Answering Services (MAS) - NYS Medicaid transportation manager for Chautauqua County
medicaid_rides.how: Call or book online at medanswering.com at least 72 hours (3 days) before a medical appointment. Trips must be approved in advance. Covers non-emergency medical trips only (bus, taxi, ambulette, or mileage payback). For emergencies call 911.

Chautauqua.other_rides: Free bus travel training from the CHQ Transit Mobility Manager: 716-661-8492. Office for the Aging / volunteer driver programs: not verified.
Chautauqua.service_hours: Mon-Fri 7 AM - 5 PM; Saturday city routes 8 AM - 5:45 PM

Erie.fares: $2.00 per ride (ages 10-64), kids under 10 free. $5 day pass, $25 7-day pass, $4 round-trip rail. With a MetGo card or the Token Transit app, fares cap at $5/day, $25/week, $75/month - after that rides are free. Cash on the bus buys a single ride only and doesn't count toward the cap.
Erie.reduced_fares: Half fare ($1.00/ride; caps $2.50/day, $12.50/week, $37.50/month) for people 65+, anyone with a Medicare card, people with qualifying disabilities (incl. SSI for serious mental illness), and Erie/Niagara Community Care child-care families. Reduced Fare MetGo card costs $2; photos taken Mon-Fri 7am-5pm at the Metropolitan Transportation Center, 181 Ellicott St. Info line 716-855-6611. Not valid on PAL.
Erie.routes_summary: Metro Bus routes across Erie and Niagara counties plus Metro Rail (light rail along Main Street, downtown Buffalo to UB South Campus). Passes sold at Metro Rail station machines, the Metropolitan Transportation Center, the airport, retail partners, and in the Token Transit / Transit apps.
Erie.demand_response: PAL (Paratransit Access Line) for people whose disability prevents using regular bus/rail: must apply and be approved. Fare $3.50 on PAL MetGo card or $4 cash; 10-trip $35, 20-trip $70; attendants and kids 9 and under free. Book by 4pm the day before (no same-day): 716-855-7239, phone reservations daily 8am-8pm, or PAL Direct online 24/7. Customer service 716-855-7268.

medicaid_rides.name: Medical Answering Services (MAS) - Erie County Medicaid Transportation
medicaid_rides.how: Medicaid members with no other way to get to a medical appointment: call MAS Mon-Fri 7am-6pm or book at medanswering.com at least 3 business days before the appointment (e.g. Monday-Wednesday appointments must be booked by the Friday before). Standing orders available for repeat trips like dialysis. Note: a 2024 state provider list gives 1-866-932-7740 for Erie - try it if the 800 number doesn't work.

Erie.other_rides: Code Blue nights (32°F or colder): call 211 to ask for outreach/transportation to the Buffalo City Mission Code Blue shelter. Southern Erie County: Rural Outreach Center van picks up from 7pm on Code Blue nights (716-240-2220 x106).
Erie.service_hours: Varies by route - check metro.nfta.com or call 716-855-7211.
Erie.office_address: Metropolitan Transportation Center, 181 Ellicott St, Buffalo, NY 14203

Niagara.agency: Connect Niagara (Niagara County DPW, formerly Niagara County Rural Transportation) plus NFTA Metro
Niagara.phone: Connect Niagara pickup reservations 716-285-9357; NFTA Metro Customer Care 716-855-7211
Niagara.fares: Connect Niagara: $2.00 on route, $4.00 off route (pickup up to 3/4 mile off the route). Transfers to other Connect Niagara routes and to NFTA Metro are free. NFTA Metro: $2.00 per ride on bus and rail.
Niagara.reduced_fares: NFTA Metro reduced fare for seniors 65+, people with disabilities, and members of the Community Care program through Erie or Niagara County. No Connect Niagara reduced fare found.
Niagara.routes_summary: Connect Niagara: Blue route Niagara Falls (Fashion Outlets) - NCCC - Sheriff's Office - Lockport (Locust & Main, Town Hall), several trips each weekday; Purple route (red route merged into it Jan 20, 2026) now stops at Niagara Falls International Airport; Gold/Green routes serve the eastern end of the county. Since Jan 2026 Connect Niagara no longer serves North Tonawanda, Wheatfield or Youngstown. NFTA Metro runs local buses in Niagara Falls and North Tonawanda and service to Buffalo; Route 59 serves Niagara Falls Airport / SUNY Niagara. Trip planner: metro.nfta.com/schedules/routes.
Niagara.demand_response: Connect Niagara route deviation: call 716-285-9357 by the end of business the day before to be picked up within 3/4 mile of a route ($4). NFTA PAL paratransit for people with disabilities (see metro.nfta.com 'Get PAL Info').

medicaid_rides.name: Medical Answering Services (MAS) - NYS Medicaid transportation
medicaid_rides.how: Call 7am-7pm any day, ahead of your appointment (book online at medanswering.com too). Covers non-emergency rides to Medicaid-covered medical visits only. For emergencies call 911.

Niagara.other_rides: Niagara County Office for the Aging medical transportation (wheelchair accessible) 716-438-4038 (2023 county guide).
Niagara.service_hours: Connect Niagara Mon-Fri except legal holidays (Blue route trips from about 6am to early evening). NFTA Customer Care phones Mon-Fri 6am-6pm.
Niagara.office_address: Connect Niagara: Niagara County DPW (address not published on route page). NFTA Metro Customer Care Center: 181 Ellicott St, Buffalo, NY 14203 (Mon-Fri 7am-5pm).

Cattaraugus.agency: Olean Area Transit System (OATS), now sponsored by Access Allegany; plus Seneca Transit System on Seneca Nation territories
Cattaraugus.phone: OATS route info / call center 585-968-0834 (Transdev, Mon-Fri 8am-8pm); Access Allegany call center 585-593-1738; Seneca Transit 585-968-0834, after hours/Saturday 585-610-6449
Cattaraugus.fares: OATS: $1 one-way within Olean; $2 between Olean and Salamanca. Cash only, exact change. 30-day pass $30 (sold at Greater Olean Area Chamber of Commerce, Seneca Nation Clerk's Office, City of Salamanca Clerk's Office, The Rehabilitation Center). Route deviation costs 2x fare. Seneca Transit: $1 within a zone, $2 between zones, +$1 per route deviation; $30 30-day pass; free transfer to OATS in Salamanca.
Cattaraugus.reduced_fares: OATS: seniors 60+ and riders with disabilities pay half ($0.50 in town, $1 Olean-Salamanca). Children ride free (Olean fare page says under 12; Salamanca page says 6 and under). Personal care attendants with an advance reservation ride free.
Cattaraugus.routes_summary: OATS Route 001 Olean City Loop; 002 Olean-Salamanca Loop (AM & PM); 003 Salamanca-Olean (AM & PM); 004 Olean Downtown Circulator; St. Bonaventure night runs while classes are in session. Routes 001-004 run Monday-Saturday. Seneca Transit runs Irving to Steamburg / Salamanca on Seneca territories, open to the public. Most of rural Cattaraugus County (Gowanda, Franklinville, Little Valley, Randolph, etc.) has no fixed bus found.
Cattaraugus.demand_response: OATS buses can deviate off-route for a doubled fare - call 585-968-0834 ahead. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles. No separate county dial-a-ride confirmed; ask Access Allegany 585-593-1738 (the Allegany and Cattaraugus systems voted toward a merger in Oct 2024).

medicaid_rides.name: Medical Answering Services (MAS) - NYS Medicaid transportation manager
medicaid_rides.how: Call or book at medanswering.com at least 3 days (72 hours) before your medical appointment. Rides must be approved ahead of time and are for non-emergency Medicaid-covered appointments only (bus pass, taxi/van, ambulette or mileage payback). For emergencies call 911.

Cattaraugus.other_rides: Cattaraugus Community Action (716-945-1041) offers transportation for domestic violence victims. Office for the Aging / volunteer drivers not verified.
Cattaraugus.service_hours: OATS Mon-Sat (exact times on the 2026 schedule PDF on salamancany.gov); call center Mon-Fri 8am-8pm. Seneca Transit info line Mon-Fri 5:30am-8pm.
Cattaraugus.office_address: City of Olean, 101 E State St, Olean, NY 14760

Allegany.fares: Fares not published in the sources found - call 585-593-1738 for rates.
Allegany.reduced_fares: Not found - ask the call center about senior, disability or student discounts.
Allegany.routes_summary: County bus routes run roughly 5am-8pm depending on route, and connect with Hornell Area Transit in Alfred. Access Allegany also sponsors OATS in Olean (Cattaraugus County). Allegany County legislature voted in Oct 2024 to merge with Cattaraugus County's system.
Allegany.demand_response: Listed as paratransit service; call 585-593-1738 to ask about scheduling a ride.

medicaid_rides.name: Medical Answering Services (MAS) - NYS Medicaid transportation manager
medicaid_rides.how: Call or book at medanswering.com at least 3 days (72 hours) before your medical appointment. Rides must be approved ahead of time and are for non-emergency Medicaid-covered appointments only (bus pass, taxi/van, ambulette or mileage payback). For emergencies call 911.

Allegany.service_hours: Call center 8am-noon and 12:30-4:30pm; buses about 5am-8pm depending on route.
Allegany.office_address: Allegany County, 7 Court St, Belmont, NY 14813 (county address from FTA transit profile)
